Since each term of \(f\) is odd, \(f(-x)=-f(x)\). Thus
\[
f(b-9)=-f(4a)=f(-4a).
\]
Also,
\[
f'(x)=\frac{2\ln 2\cdot 2^x}{(2^x+1)^2}+1+\cos x>0,
\]
so \(f\) is strictly increasing, hence injective. Therefore
\[
b-9=-4a \implies 4a+b=9.
\]
Now minimize
\[
\frac1a+\frac1b
\]
subject to \(4a+b=9\), \(a,b>0\). By Cauchy,
\[
\left(\frac1a+\frac1b\right)(4a+b)\ge (2+1)^2=9.
\]
Since \(4a+b=9\),
\[
\frac1a+\frac1b\ge 1.
\]
Equality occurs when \(b=2a\), and with \(4a+b=9\), this gives \(a=\frac32,\ b=3\). Therefore the minimum value is
\[
\boxed{1}.
\]
